title: Actions to Track Originators of Fake News of Partial Lockdown
what_it_is: Actions to Track Originators of Fake News of Partial Lockdown

sections.label: Police action on COVID-19 falsehoods
sections.summary: Police investigate falsehoods about COVID-19, including a man charged for a false lockdown message carrying up to three years' jail, S$10,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police take a serious view of all reports of falsehoods regarding the COVID-19 situation, including those that claim “partial lockdown”, as these may cause public alarm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Police will investigate such cases and take firm action against the culprits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For instance, Police identified a 40-year-old man who allegedly circulated a false message claiming that he had "intel" that the Government would close all coffee shops and food courts, and open supermarkets only two days a week.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The man was charged on 27 April 2020 for an offence of communicating a false message under the Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This carries an imprisonment term of up to three years, a fine of up to S$10,000, or both.

sections.label: Government clarifications on lockdown rumour
sections.summary: The Government clarified the partial lockdown rumour via the Gov.sg WhatsApp channel and MOH website, and perpetrators will be taken to task.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: In this case, the Government has issued a clarification via the Gov.sg WhatsApp channel on the same day that the rumour of the partial lockdown was circulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: A clarification was also issued on the MOH website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: But I think the point Mr Lim Biow Chuan made is very clear – that we will not go easy, we will not take this lightly and perpetrators, if caught, will be taken to task.

sections.label: Assessing false message charges
sections.summary: Each false message case is assessed on investigation findings, and the Public Prosecutor decides the most appropriate charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Every case of communication of false message is assessed based on the findings rising from investigations and the Public Prosecutor exercises his discretion on the most appropriate charge.
